sources.entry: jevme - Voice control for any Mac app that acts while you're still talking and learns from its own AI decisions.

summary.one_liner: jevme is a macOS voice-control app that carries out spoken commands in any app while you are still talking, using a fast classifier and memoizing slower LLM decisions for reuse.
summary.what_it_does: Streams live speech from the Mac microphone through Apple's speech recognizer and routes each partial transcript to the TypeSafe Jev classifier, which picks a built-in tool or hands off to an agent. Completed clauses of a sentence run in spoken order while the user keeps talking, and "stop" cancels queued work. A 35-tool shortcut catalog covers opening and quitting apps, site and Google searches, media keys, tabs, volume and dark mode. For other tasks, an agent reads the front window through macOS Accessibility and clicks, types, or presses keys step by step, with a Claude Haiku screenshot fallback when no controls are exposed. Claude Opus writes new AppleScript/JXA/shell tools or composes replies when asked, and results are saved locally as UI cases, task recipes and learned tools so repeated requests take a faster path. Generated scripts pass a policy check, compile check and Jev review, and risky actions wait for a spoken confirmation.
use_cases: voice control of a Mac without touching the keyboard
open apps and websites by speaking commands
click buttons, links or tabs by describing them
dictate or compose replies, summaries or code in an open app
automate repeated multi-step tasks on the desktop by replaying learned recipes
teach a Mac assistant a new command by demonstration
how_to_run: curl -LsSf (uv installer) | sh  # installs uv, which installs Python 3.12
git clone the repo and cd jevme
./run.sh setup  # installs deps, creates .env, checks keys and permissions
./run.sh start  # start in background; ./run.sh doctor checks permissions and keys
uv run jevme  # or run in the foreground
notable: Executes commands clause by clause while the user is still speaking, rather than waiting for the sentence to end
Memoizes slow LLM reasoning into fast classifier cases, so repeated tasks get cheaper and faster over time
Learns from demonstration: when the agent fails, it records the user's clicks (role and label only, never typed text)
Generated tools must pass a hard safety policy, compile check and Jev review before running
Personalizes speech recognition with on-screen control names and learned vocabulary
caveats: Requires macOS 14+ and Accessibility, Microphone, Speech Recognition and Screen Recording permissions granted to the launching app
Needs a paid TypeSafe API key, and an Anthropic key is recommended; without it, it falls back to the slower signed-in claude CLI
Uses cloud model calls for everything except local speech recognition and accessibility reads
